theorem_title: Geometric no-return for the power-two wall trace
formal_statement: theorem AngelDevil.wallTrace_never_returns (D : AngelDevil.DevilStrategy) (hnice : AngelDevil.Nice 2 D) (n : Nat) (hn : 0 < n) : AngelDevil.wallTrace D n ≠ AngelDevil.initialWall := by sorry
natural_language_statement: Against every Nice Devil of power two, the specified boundary-walking strategy never encounters its initial directed wall at any positive wall-transition index. The initial wall is the east side of square (-1,0). The trace uses two wall transitions per Angel turn and the obstacle set after that turn's Devil move. This is the geometric no-return obligation underlying the escape argument; it does not assume non-repetition or escape.
source: Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins (2007), https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript pp. 6-8, octagonal wall-following rule, Claim 3.1 analogue, Proposition 4.3 and Theorem 4.5. Two wall transitions per turn give an admissible power-two implementation; no-return is the remaining geometric obligation.
